Messages.Author: De Nada
Messages.Body:
On the errata for Return to Innocence, when it says
"Burn this card if this vampire loses any blood or goes to
torpor, or if your Prey is ousted." Does that mean if I have
a blood doll on my Return'd Vampire and remove a blood
I get to then burn him and bleed my prey for his capacity
during my next untap phase ?

Messages.Author: The Lasombra
Messages.Body:
In article <4SNw5.22$Y24....@nnrp1.sbc.net>,


No, it means you Burn the Card (RtI) with no effect.

The card has to be in play at the start of your next
untap phase for it to have any effect on the game.

The sentence you quote is designed to be the defense
mechanism for your prey. If they can Cryptic Mission,
Jar the Soul, Bum's Rush, or otherwise remove blood
from the vampire that played the RtI, they do not lose
the pool that RtI would have caused.

Full text of the card (errata):

"Return to Innocence [AH] - Action (4)
New card text: "Bleed. If you successfully bleed your Prey for one or
more, put this card on the acting vampire. Burn this card if this

vampire loses any blood or goes to torpor, or if your Prey is ousted.

During your next untap, this vampire is removed from play and your Prey
burns X pool, where X is the capacity of this vampire." [RTR 19980707]"

http://www.white-wolf.com/VTES/rulings.html

Carpe noctem.

Lasombra

http://members.tripod.com/~Lasombra

Sent via Deja.com http://www.deja.com/
Before you buy.

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
"De Nada" <a...@media.net> wrote:
> On the errata for Return to Innocence, when it says
> "Burn this card if this vampire loses any blood or goes to
> torpor, or if your Prey is ousted." Does that mean if I have
> a blood doll on my Return'd Vampire and remove a blood
> I get to then burn him and bleed my prey for his capacity
> during my next untap phase ?

It would mean that, if you were able to keep the vampire
around until your Master Phase to pull a blood off of him
via the Blood Doll.

As it is, the vampire (assuming the RtI is unburned) will be
removed from the game on your next untap phase, before you
get a chance to use the Blood Doll.

I don't understand your point. What if someone in your playgroup had lots
of real RtIs? How does it help play-balance to limit a deckbuilding choice
to the fanatic collector/players?

It sounds like what you're really trying to say is that RtI is only too
unbalanced if not card-limited, which is probably arguable but a different
thing than saying it shouldn't be proxied. If you're going to allow the
original RtI but card-limit it, use the same card limits for everyone in
the group rather than depending on "ecomomic card limits".

but just say, "be reasonable". Unless they wanted to deliberately duplicate

It plays the game by the rules? Besides, I think he's talking about a
group that as a whole has relatively few cards, and never did any of
the manic trading. In this case, just saying "ok, don't proxy it,
just play with what you got" will provide a pretty good impression of
what RtI does, why it was banned, and help with the top paragraph
about coping with huge bleeds. =)

We permit proxies in Atlanta, as long as you don't go apeshit on any
'very good' card. If you want to proxy 10 Disarms or 10 Tier of
Souls, for example, we're going to frown on that a little bit, since
EVERYONE would love to have 10 Disarms and, while it's fun, we would
really prefer to see you make decks out of cards that you HAVE, as
opposed to speculating wildly about cards you may NEVER have. If you
want to proxy 10 Disarms to test out a deck for a tournament, that's
different - especially if you have a way to borrow and/or get the 10
lined up, if you like your idea. And if you want to proxy 15
Malkavian Time Auctions or the like, (i did), go for it, since the
card is so marginally useful anyway. =) We proxy Embraces on a
regular basis (Mike Perlman uses sleeved Pokemon cards to represent
them - which is VERY convenient, since now the Embraces have names and
can be referred to by such instead of "Um, third from the left with
one blood and the Vicissitude card."), for example.

Basically, we believe that you should more or less just play with the
cards you got. This doesn't hurt play balance, as NL is inherently
balanced. It does mean that I can't make a 10-Disarm deck. Rats. If
I really want to make a 10-Disarm deck, I ought to get 10 Disarms. We
have done all kinds of lending back and forth around here on previous
occasions - in fact, someone still has all my Brujah Debates, come to
think of it. But I have 7 of his Mark of Damnations, so it's no
biggie. If you play with proxies for some of the ultra-rare Sabbat
cards, though, it tends to disturb people - esp. when NOBODY in the
group has enough to make such a deck.

-- Derek

Correct. It doesn't really affect play balance AT ALL, although the
guy who consistently has 2 DIs in every deck IS going to have a small
advantage. Should we let people freely proxy DI, then? Would YOU?
We feel that DI was difficult enough to get that it ought to matter
SOME - again, the whole concept of CCGs in the first place is "play
with the cards you got". V:TES is great, in that the guy without THAT
many cards is capable of competing with the guy with multiple DIs and
fifty-rare decks. We see it ALL the time in our group.

>>We permit proxies in Atlanta, as long as you don't go apeshit on any

It gives us an incentive to actually GET the cards ourselves, instead
of just printing out copies of whatever we need on a color printer and
sticking them in sleeves. Mr. Suitcase is welcome to come play with
us anytime he wants to, and if he has 10 Disarms, good for him. We
aren't going to worry about it very much, nor are we suddenly going to
let ourselves start proxying 10 Disarms in a deck.

If you allow unlimited proxies, nobody bothers to buy any cards, and
the game rots for lack of sales. Bad idea. But the occasional proxy
for experimental or entertainment value? Sure, no problem.

>I've also never found a 'very good' card I'd want to use 10 of. I have
>a couple of very rare cards (Sabbat rares) I use over and over in a couple
>of decks I have but they're not the classic chase cards. (I guess LoP
>would qualify in this category, too.) Like rich desserts, there's on so
>many Direct Interventions, Dreams of the Sphinx, Protected Resources, War
>Ghouls, Succubi, Disarms, and so forth a deck can stomach. Thankfully.

Hm. Don Cruez, Donal O'Connor, Constanza Vinti... Torn Signpost,
Immortal Grapple, Disarm, Amaranth. Minion Tap/5th as blood gain to
get all of them out. Several Archon votes to provide the Rush
actions, and Bum's Rush or Bloodhunt cards to get rid of opposing
voters who can't be talked into voting your way on the Amaranth. A
few Flashes to chase people down. Six Conditionings, to provide the
"oust punch". I could see putting 10 Disarms in that deck, no
problem. Nobody in our group wants to see it unless I actually GET
the 10 Disarms, though, and I wouldn't blame them one bit.

Uhh... Torn Signpost, Immortal Grapple, Disarm will torporize anyone
who can't prevent 3 points of damage, hit for 3 themselves, or do
aggravated hand damage. That's only 3 cards for the combo, and there
are NOT that many decks out there that can get around it. It might be
time to borrow/steal the Disarms necessary to build this and take it
to the next tournament, just as an experiment - I don't think
Fortitude has been putting in much of an appearance these days either.

So let's see, 10 Signposts, 10 Grapples, 10 Disarms, 6 Minion Tap, 6
5th Tradition, 4 Archon, 6 Bum's Rush, 8 Flash, 6 Conditioning...
let's see, we're up to 66 cards. 8 Amaranth for 74. Need six more
cards - take your pick. Barrens, Elder Library, Fraggie make 3, and
probably 3 Alacrity cards would be a good idea as well. That's an 80
card library, and fairly functional. To slim it down and make a good
chance of drawing your stuff, drop 2 each of the Signpost, Grapple,
and Disarm, and drop 1 Minion Tap, 1 5th, 1 Archon, and 1 Alacrity.
Now you've got a nasty little 70 card wonder, although it is somewhat
combat light and can only burn 8 vampires - better pick carefully.

Crypt is easy. 3 Don, 3 Constanza, 3 Donal, and 3 of ...well, take
your pick. Anvil fits in there best - he can't do the 5th, but he is
cheap, has the full skillset, and adds to the voting power a little.
Want to go big? Ulugh Beg has pot/cel/DOM, although you probably
don't want him fighting since he only punches for 2. If you want, you
can even go Angelica, with POT/DOM/cel - 3 more votes, but she can't
do the 5th either and is kind of big.

No, I think there'd be plenty of room for 10 Disarms. Especially if
you go up to a 90 card deck, when you have room for all kinds of
additional toys to help out. =)

prey. Wakes or more like Forced Awakening. Intercept - I usually like
KCRG-type things in a deck that doesn't feature auspex but Sport Bikes
are another way to go.

And I'm not sure there's enough rush in this deck, old 6. You might
want to throw in some Haven Uncovereds, which work very well with
torporizing decks (they can't get rid of the Havens in torpor, hence
they're a pain to remove as they come out of torpor).

I'd be very surprised if this deck wound up with 10 Disarms after you
got through tuning it. Even with 90 cards.

Fred

None of us are willing to spend ridiculous amounts of money on the
game, however. Given THAT limitation, it begins to make a little more
sense, yes? Many of us were drawn in when Jyhad boxes were $5 each
from the Edgeman (in bulk) - as such, we have a huge chunk of cards,
but really haven't blown our wallets on the game. Chasing Disarms at
the odds of one per box of Sabbat is just ridiculous. And nobody is

>Yea, but you're talking about running some other stuff, too: the Minion
>Tap/5th tradition, the rushes to get the chance to torporize, and that

>in 10 of the finisher card of a 3-card combat combo.

Minion Tap and 5th don't have to happen on the same turn. If I get
Don Cruez out first with a Minion Tap in hand, I'll yank him down to
3-4 and leave him there for awhile until I see a 5th. If someone
makes him go away, OH WELL, HE COST FOUR. And in the meantime, he can
be beating things up waiting for his 5th, since if I don't have a 5th
in hand, I must have all my combat... and with only 6 5ths in the
deck, I'm not going to worry about hand jamming on them. Hand jamming
on MT is a laugher, since it's much worse to be stuck with a handful
of combat and no pool than it is to have a handful of pool and no
combat.

Rushes will only hurt if I can't get to an Archon fast enough. I
should be able to pass an Archon with a little table management and
the amount of votes that can land on the table. Once the first Archon
hits the table, I have one guaranteed Rush action per turn, which is
usually all you -need-. 3-card combat combos are ridiculously easy to
pull off if you include enough cards in the deck, and there just
aren't that many other cards in there. Probably too many Flashes,
really, but those maneuvers will matter.

>>So let's see, 10 Signposts, 10 Grapples, 10 Disarms, 6 Minion Tap, 6
>>5th Tradition, 4 Archon, 6 Bum's Rush, 8 Flash, 6 Conditioning...
>
>That's too many Disarms. The signposts you need the most of. (Or were
>some of the vamps + hand damage?) The grapples are mainly there to hold
>down the S:CEs, since you don't have any extra strikes (and I suspect
>this deck wants extra strikes) so 10 is probably too many. Otherwise,
>the presses to continue aren't nearly as fun.

Both the Signposts and the Disarms are equally crucial. It does me no
good to strike for 3 without ripping their arm off. It also does me
no good to strike for 1 and have a Disarm in hand. The grapples are
there both to hold down S:CE and Dodge, and to provide some combat
defense against the wack decks (Coma, Entombment come to mind), or any
other deck that might want to pull some strange strike or other out of
its ass. Grapple solves both that AND half of the Disarm requirements
- if you're not playing Potence, then I grab you and you're striking
for 1 point of hand damage, or 2 with Lucky Blow/Scorpion Sting. I
can see Protean and Vicissitude coming a mile away, so I can take some
extra care for those decks.

So, I need equal numbers of all the above. 10, 10, 10. Hence the
Barrens, Fraggie, and Elder - I want to be able to go fishing for all
the cards if necessary, although since it's only 3 cards i'm likely to
have them in hand lots.

>>let's see, we're up to 66 cards. 8 Amaranth for 74. Need six more

remember this number ^^^^^^^^^^

>>cards - take your pick. Barrens, Elder Library, Fraggie make 3, and
>>probably 3 Alacrity cards would be a good idea as well.
>
>Hunting grounds. Ancilla Empowerments (as I discovered at Gencon) to

What the FRO do i want hunting grounds for? My guys are gaining large

thing that costs blood in the deck is Conditioning... a wopping 1.
Oh, and I'm probably getting punched for 1 each combat.

Ancilla Empowerment wouldn't make a bad 3-card inclusion. Bag the 3
Alacrities and add those instead - odds are you'll never have more
than 3 guys out with this deck anyway.

>hold off weeny decks. Information Highway. Sudden Reversals to hold

Info Highway only good in this deck if you draw it first turn. No
good anytime after that - waste of space. 5th/MT blood gain by my
prey won't get off more than once, IF that, before I burn that vampire
and stop all that shit, so I don't care that much. Dead guys commit
no Traditions.

I should worry about tap & bleed more, but hell, I don't have enough
minions to piss around trying to block Samson and Ohanna, or to waste
time trying to Deflect them all. I might as well just add some more
"kill" to the deck, and off them first. None of my guys will be
untapped ANYWAY.

>off Tap & Bleed preditors and 5th/Minion tap blood gaining by your
>prey. Wakes or more like Forced Awakening. Intercept - I usually like
>KCRG-type things in a deck that doesn't feature auspex but Sport Bikes
>are another way to go.

Dead guys don't do things worth intercepting, or worth Waking for.
Now you know why I am worried about the slimmed down version only
having 8 full combats in it - I may need to make more than 8 dead
guys.

>And I'm not sure there's enough rush in this deck, old 6. You might

Not just 6 Rush cards. The 4 Archons provides a nasty lot of Rush,
and also handles a lot of the pesky diablerie problem - although with
8 built-in votes in the deck, it probably doesn't have as much of a
problem, especially if it threatens/rushes voters first.

>want to throw in some Haven Uncovereds, which work very well with
>torporizing decks (they can't get rid of the Havens in torpor, hence
>they're a pain to remove as they come out of torpor).

except if you notice, i have a lot of Amaranth in there. Diablerie is
featured heavily in this deck. Burned vampires take no actions.

>I'd be very surprised if this deck wound up with 10 Disarms after you
>got through tuning it. Even with 90 cards.

What good would it do with being able to kill any less than 10
vampires? Its whole idea is "make stuff dead". =)

>What good would it do with being able to kill any less than 10
>vampires? Its whole idea is "make stuff dead". =)

Yea my experience is that it typically doesn't work that way in
collectable card games. You assume you can use all 10 but since they're
the finisher card, there will be times during the game (LOTS of times
if you're not particularly lucky), when the Disarms will show up and jam
your hand and you'll be dumping them hand over fist. There will be other
times you couldn't draw one to save your life. It usually turns out to
just be easier to put a bunch of different types of combat cards (signposts,
potence strikes, extra strike cards, immortal grapples, even dodges or
dodge-with-an-additional-strike) in that will allow you to combo them
effectively in whatever order they turn up in. You can frequently
acheive the torporizing just through non-Disarm but otherwise favorable
combats and all your Amaranth, Archon diablerizing stuff is just as useful.
You still want SOME Disarms because they're still incredibly useful - as
long the other stuff is always on hand. So you wind up reducing their
number and using other cards instead.

Anyway, that's always been my experience. Conceiving of how powerful 10
Disarms could be in a deck and actually making the cards turn up in
optimal order against opponents who don't have any defense against it
is one thing. Seeing how often that happens in real life is another.

Fred

Not having to worry about anyone bleeding for tons at any given moment
is a very handy thing. A good vote deck ought to have enough pool
gain to deal with consistent multiple bleeds for 1 or 2, and PR
ensures that you won't be seeing anything more than that - permitting
you to dump a ton of Deflections and Wakes. Putting 4 in a 90-card
deck ensures that you'll get one fairly early, and it also ensures
that if you need to bleed for 1 to make an oust, that you can toss PR
back out afterwards and regain your defense. =)

(shrug) We are recruiting new players actively, and we have quite a
few who've joined us over the past year or so - none of the new
players wants to go out and blow wads of cash on cards (although we've
offered them the opportunity by telling them about the $250 Sabbat
boxes on ebay =), they want to LEARN first. I can't speak DIRECTLY
for the other players in my group, but I do know how they think and
some about them. They have the cash on hand to successfully chase
Disarms or the like in a 'brute force' manner - they MUCH prefer to do
it the "trade, network, network, wait a long time" way. I can't blame
them at all. =)

Sure, I'd have trade bait then for other cards (the rest of the box),
but I really kind of cringe at the thought of throwing money at a

USUALLY) kill though, and that's not a good purpose in this deck. It

POT/PRE bruise-and-bleed that just has a big pile of Signposts, Undead

myself. =) I also don't see people choosing to enter combat with me
unless they can poke me in the eye, especially after they lose one
vampire.

>need more Signposts than the other two. Nothing else works without
>them - or some other means to have a better-than-even exchange with your

Signposts, so they don't know whether or not they'll get bopped ahead
of time, and so I won't waste cards when they have enough maneuvers in
hand. But again, a simple 3/1 exchange is just not a useful action
for this deck to take, unless 3 can put the guy in torpor. It serves

Library, and -get- the 3 cards I need.

>>I can see Protean and Vicissitude coming a mile away, so I can take

>
>What "extra care" can you take just because you see it coming? The deck
>totally depends on having good things happen in combat. I don't see
>anything other than the Flash Maneuvers that will allow you to do anything

Every deck has a weakness, and agg hand damage is usually a Potence
deck's Achilles heel. I could get frantic trying to stop them, which
would add even more moving parts to the deck and reduce its ability to
make things dead.... or I could just figure "ok, i'll be screwed if my
prey is Gangrel". If my predator is Gangrel, I can just refuse to

from them. That's about the only care I can take, but (shrug) it
happens.

Hunting Grounds are NOT always good - they cost pool and a Master
action. I'm fairly light on Master actions in this deck, so that's no
big deal, but the 2 pool could be very expensive. The blood gain via
MT is sufficient, but there ARE only 6 in the deck, so I won't be
consistently Incredibly Bloating Up - especially if I want to get a
10-cap and two 8-caps out.

With 5th, and the fact that I'll be diablerizing/amaranthing vampires
with blood on them, I should have plenty of ways to put blood back on
the vampires. A HG would be an extra moving part that might keep me
from getting the IG/US/Disarm in hand. (Also, I probably WANT my guys
to get fairly low on occasion, to make me feel like the 5ths actually
matter. =)

>>Info Highway only good in this deck if you draw it first turn. No
>>good anytime after that - waste of space.
>
>I disagree. With the Minion Tap/5th combo, you could run into a sudden
>windfall of pool at any time during the game.

I've only got 6 Minion Taps, and I hope to be playing with ~26 pool
worth of vampires. =) Also realizing that some of my defense is
"shrug off your predator via blood gain", I don't want to dip into
things TOO far.

There's another point - a sudden windfall of pool doesn't benefit me
much. I only have 4 different vampires in my crypt. There's only so
many I can get out. =)

>>5th/MT blood gain by my prey won't get off more than once, IF that,
>>before I burn that vampire and stop all that shit, so I don't care
>>that much. Dead guys commit no Traditions.
>

It won't always work, but the trick is in what you can do when it's
NOT available. If it's not available, that must be because I have
other cards in my hand. What other cards could I have in my hand?
Well, a MT, or a 5th, or a Conditioning, or a hand-cycler master, or
an Archon/Ancilla Empowerment, or a Flash, or an Amaranth. All of
these cards are playable (except the Flash/Amaranth, but those are
freely discardable) without the combat in hand AND will do useful
things when they are played, even if I don't have the combat yet. It
helps that it's only 3 cards, so I will usually ALWAYS have two in my
hand and be chasing just one. =) It also helps that I'm at an
80-card deck (with 10/10/10) or a 70-card deck (with 8/8/8), and THAT
increases the odds of me seeing them as well just because there ain't
enough cards to get in my WAY. With a 70-card deck, you are always
looking at 10% of your deck in your hand. =) With the
Barrens/Fraggie/EL, you are in VERY good shape when you NEED to just
move cards around.

The biggest problem I worry about is, of course, getting to the Rush
actions and getting into combat. If that happens consistently enough,
I won't have a problem keeping the combo cards in hand or near to my
hand, and won't have a problem just taking other actions as they
appear in my hand and/or are appropriate.

Except when you do this, you often end up with a deck that has a pile
of glop in it and can't consistently put ANYTHING in torpor. We see a
lot of mid-range vampires (5-7) around here, usually supported by a
number of small ones, and that's what this deck is designed to be most
effective against. It kills the big guy first and erases him forever.
Then it deals with the little ones as it sees fit, since usually
dropping someone's 7-cap puts a huge crimp in their strategy.

The problem with lots of multiple cards is that you don't decrease the
difficulty of getting a good combo in hand. Torn Signpost/IG/Blur is
great and will vaporize someone's head, but it's still 3 cards. Torn
Signpost/IG/Undead Strength is much less great, and still 3 cards.
Torn Signpost/Acrobatics/Pushing the Limit is nice, but it's 3 cards,
and people S:CE away from it. And if I have an Acrobatics/IG/Undead
Strength in my hand, I probably feel small and silly since I can't
even get all 3 of those to move.
